highlights.title: Network & Solution Design
highlights.description: Multi-site networks designed to a client brief: routing, site-to-site VPN, DMZ and Wi-Fi, sized around the equipment already in place (Cisco IOS, Packet Tracer).

highlights.title: Security Engineering
highlights.description: Intrusion detection and prevention on edge hardware (Snort 3, ML/DL), and hands-on offensive testing of Wi-Fi, SSH and ROS-based robots.

highlights.title: Embedded & IoT Prototyping
highlights.description: Raspberry Pi, ESP32 and Arduino builds taken from idea to working demo: sensors, motor control, computer vision and web control apps.

highlights.title: Applied ML & Computer Vision
highlights.description: Models for intrusion detection, GNSS interference, antenna classification and vision-based control, benchmarked and deployed on constrained hardware.

highlights.title: Data & Reporting
highlights.description: Power BI dashboards, ETL, quarterly reports and process manuals that turn operational data into something decision-makers can act on.

highlights.title: Communication & Leadership
highlights.description: Conference talks, live product demos and team leadership: led the Batterly and voice-controlled chair builds and ran every student club as Clubs Director.

paragraphs: I'm a Telecommunication & IoT engineer. I like working across the whole of a connected system: the network, the hardware at the edge, the software and machine learning on top, and the security that holds it together. I graduated from the University of Wollongong in Dubai with First Class Honours (GPA 3.7/4.0) and the Top Graduate Award.

My thesis, AstraIPS, runs AI-based intrusion prevention on a Raspberry Pi 5. It placed 1st of 89 at the UOWD Research Competition and was accepted in IEEE Access. I also led the team behind Batterly, a pancake printer we built for the B2B market at a fraction of what existing machines cost, and showed it live at an innovation fair.

I've presented my papers at international conferences, and I enjoy that part as much as the build: explaining what a system does and why it's worth having. Right now I'm a Research Assistant at UOWD, using machine learning to detect GNSS spoofing and jamming.
